slides.prompt: Fill in the mechanism passed as the second argument to cv.wait() to protect against spurious wakeups.
slides.codeSnippet:
cv.wait(lock, []() { return dataReady; });

slides.title: Lock Type Requirement for condition_variable
slides.prompt: Why does std::condition_variable::wait requiring std::unique_lock<std::mutex> instead of std::lock_guard<std::mutex>?
options: The wait method must unlock and re-lock the mutex internally while suspending execution
lock_guard does not support template instantiation with condition variables
It is an arbitrary design choice with no functional difference
slides.correctAnswer: The wait method must unlock and re-lock the mutex internally while suspending execution

slides.title: Condition Variable Any Type
slides.prompt: Fill in the variant class that works with any lock type beyond std::unique_lock<std::mutex>.
slides.codeSnippet: std::___ cv_any; // Works with custom lock types

slides.title: Spurious Wakeup Definition
slides.prompt: What is a spurious wakeup in multithreaded programming?
options: A thread waiting on a condition variable wakes up without any notify call being made
A thread crashes due to a lost notification signal
A deadlock caused by out-of-order notification
A notify_all call that fails to reach suspended threads
slides.correctAnswer: A thread waiting on a condition variable wakes up without any notify call being made

slides.title: Timed Waiting on CV
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to wait on a condition variable until a specific time point.

slides.title: Lost Wakeup Hazard
slides.prompt: How does using a predicate with cv.wait() prevent lost wakeups?
options: It checks the boolean condition before sleeping, preventing sleep if the signal was sent early
It queues notifications so no signal is lost
It locks the condition variable directly
It forces the notifier to block until the signal is consumed
slides.correctAnswer: It checks the boolean condition before sleeping, preventing sleep if the signal was sent early
